root_cause.text: The code was checking the hardware DC6 state (via hardware register read) instead of the software-tracked DC6 state when deciding whether to call `intel_dmc_update_dc6_allowed_count()`, causing the function to be invoked before DMC initialization completes, resulting in a NULL pointer dereference.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes two locations from reading the hardware DC_STATE_EN register (`val & DC_STATE_EN_UPTO_DC6` and `intel_de_read(display, DC_STATE_EN) & DC_STATE_EN_UPTO_DC6`) to using the software-tracked state (`power_domains->dc_state & DC_STATE_EN_UPTO_DC6`). The CVE description explicitly states: "Thus, using the HW DC6 state is incorrect and it also leads to the above oops. Fix both issues by using the SW DC6 state for the tracking." The hardware state can be enabled by BIOS without the DMC firmware being loaded, but the software state is only set after proper initialization, preventing premature calls to `intel_dmc_update_dc6_allowed_count()` when `dmc` is still NULL.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix DC6 state tracking by using cached power domain state instead of potentially stale register value to correctly detect state transitions.
intent_record.what: Changed the source of the dc6_was_enabled flag assignment from `val` (a local register read variable) to `power_domains->dc_state` (the cached state structure member).
intent_record.how: This ensures that dc6_was_enabled reflects the previously stored DC state rather than the current hardware register value. This prevents a race condition where the hardware register might have been updated between the initial read and this check, causing incorrect logic flow in the DC6 state transition decision.

intent_record.intent_summary: Replace direct hardware register read with cached dc_state value to reduce I/O overhead in DC6 allowed count check.
intent_record.what: Replaced a direct hardware register read `intel_de_read(display, DC_STATE_EN)` with a cached value from `power_domains->dc_state` when checking the DC6 enabled state.
intent_record.how: This change uses a previously cached DC state value instead of performing a new hardware register read operation. This reduces I/O overhead and latency by avoiding a register access, relying instead on a maintained in-memory copy of the DC state that should be kept synchronized with hardware state.
